elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 permits PB to terminate the Agreement "at any time" without cause, subject to notice.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 requires ninety (90) days' prior written notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Upon Customer's convenience termination, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund is provided. Instead, PB must pay SFJ 150% of Development Costs and may remain liable for certain Approval Payments.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered language gives SFJ only event-triggered termination rights following a Change of Control or specified JSC disagreement; it does not grant SFJ a general termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 permits PB to terminate the Agreement "at any time" without cause.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 requires ninety (90) days' prior written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: PB must pay 150% of all Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ before termination. That payment is not capped at three months' fees, regardless of its characterization as consideration for the Trial Data Package.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted, so there is no such right exercisable before the end of a term. SFJ's stated rights require specific Change-of-Control or JSC-disagreement triggers and are not general convenience rights.

elements.element: Vendor's convenience termination requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor convenience right is present. Moreover, each stated discretionary, event-triggered SFJ termination right expressly requires at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice.

result.reason: The redline creates a workable PB at-will termination right on 90 days' written notice and removes the $60 million spend gate, satisfying the fallback notice mechanics. It fails the preferred position because notice is not 30 days and no pro-rata refund is provided. It also fails the fallback because the required 150% of Development Costs is not capped at three months' fees. The added notice periods for SFJ's event-triggered termination rights do not impose the fallback's end-of-term limitation, although those rights are not themselves convenience rights. The redline is not minimal because it modifies separate Change-of-Control and JSC termination provisions without curing the dispositive fee defect. The remaining provisions are generally coherent and no direct contradiction is introduced.
